Nyasha, you are right. We need to see it to believe it. I have generated images of the three different scenarios so you can decide which path is the "Greyway" path.

Here is the visual breakdown of the problem and the two solutions we discussed.

### **1\. The Problem: The "Placebo" (Current State)**

This is what "John" faces right now. He drags in his 60 images, and then he has to manually click "Use" 60 times. It is slow, tedious, and if he has too many images, the browser will crash and he'll lose everything.

![][image1]

### **2\. The Solution: The "Greyway Patch" (Less Confusing One)**

This is the solution I recommend for "John." We modify the create.html file to add a **"Batch Actions"** toolbar. John drags his images in, clicks **one button** ("Insert All as Animation"), and the tool automatically writes the code for him. It also stops the browser from crashing by keeping large files in memory.

![][image2]

### **3\. The Alternative: The "Developer Way" (Technical)**

This is the "localhost" method. You don't import any images into the tool. Instead, you run a small server (the black window in the background) and tell WoofJS where to find the files on your computer. This is very efficient and has no limits, but it is too technical for the average user.

![][image3]

Nyasha, **Image 2** is the one we want. It solves the problem for the average user ("John") without forcing them to become a developer.
